pages.text: Each frog trait has two parts called alleles. One allele comes from one parent, and one allele comes from the other parent. This is the heart of $(l:zen_amphibia:genetics/dna_basics)frog DNA$(/l).
This is why two normal-looking frogs can sometimes make a surprising $(l:zen_amphibia:lifecycle/tadpoles)tadpole$(/l). A parent may carry a useful allele even if that frog is not your best producer.

A carrier is a frog worth keeping because it hides a trait you may want later. Do not judge every frog by what it does right now; sometimes its children reveal the treasure. See $(l:zen_amphibia:genetics/breeding_goals)Breeding Goals$(/l).
